name: Comites Catafractarii Bucellarii iuniores

abilities.name: Flying Wedge
abilities.text: The unit moves into a flying wedge-shaped attack formation.

abilities.name: Steady
abilities.text: Improves the unit's ability to defend at the cost of their mobility.

abilities.name: Raise Banner
abilities.text: Increases your general's area of influence and improves the army's defence for an extended period.

abilities.name: Trample
abilities.text: Charges are more effective for an extended time.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Bucellarii (Latin Bucellarius) - personal bodyguards of private figures - military commanders, senators in the Eastern and Western Roman Empires. This term appeared in the late 4th or the beginning of the 5th century. Buccellarii were copied from barbarian retinue and replaced the Comites. Bucellarii were strictly mounted warriors. The Latin word Boukellaton meant «dry, dried, toasted bread with a hole in the middle». The reason for this nickname was that the bucellarii were attended to their lord's meals and could eat wheat bread, which was more tasty and less rough than the bread given to common soldiers. Bucellarii were entirely dependent on their patron, who supplied them with food, horses and weapons, and had the right to both reward and punish them. It is impossible to consider bucellarii as mere mercenaries: they were «taken as companions»; they swore an oath to their dominus and in their oath also mentioned the name of the Emperor; in battle they did not leave their dominus and defended him to the last drop of blood, and in case he was treacherously killed outside the battle, avenged his death. This is how Flavius Aetius' death was avenged by his bucellarius Optila, who killed Emperor Valentinian III in 455.
history: Having faced the deadly Parthian cataphracts at Carrhae, come off worse, and then struggled against the awesome crushing strength of the Sarmatian lancers, it wasn't long before the Roman army was tailoring its own cavalry to match, despite resisting the idea for some time. Gradually, Rome began to integrate its own versions, the catafractarii and clibinarii, into the Legions. They were probably first fielded during the reign of the Emperor Hadrian, as an auxiliary force of Gauls and Pannonians. However, despite their general success, it was the 4th century AD before catafractarii became a permanent addition to the ranks, possibly due to Macrinus' catastrophic defeat at Nisibis in AD217, by the Parthians. Covered head-to-foot in scale or mail armour, and armed with lances, it is clear that the 'iron horsemen' were the forerunners to the more familiar knights of the Medieval age.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
